\[
\hat{R} =
\begin{cases}
m & C_I \le C_u \\
m\,W + z\,(1 - W),\quad W = e^{-K \frac{C_I - C_u}{C_{\max} - C_I}} & C_u < C_I < C_{\max} \\
z & C_I \ge C_{\max}
\end{cases},
\qquad
C_{\max} = \sqrt{1 + 2 C_u^2}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(C_I\): The coefficient of variation of the window
- \(C_u\): The coefficient of variation of the speckle
- \(C_{\max}\): The upper class limit
- \(K\): The damping

Lopes, Touzi and Nezry split the image into three classes by the local coefficient of variation C_I. Below C_u the window is pure speckle, so the output is the mean m. Above C_max it holds a strong target or edge, so the pixel z is kept. Between, the weight W blends the two, with the damping K. C_max = sqrt(1 + 2 C_u^2) is the largest variation pure speckle is expected to reach.
